content.intro: This lesson covers function calling and tool use through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Use schema-constrained outputs and tool calls as a controlled application protocol. A model request is a proposal, not proof that an external action is authorized or completed.
content.why_it_matters: What tool calling is describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next.

items.title: Model-generated tool requests
items.text: Model-generated tool requests belongs to the application integration boundary. Validate inputs before sending them, keep credentials on the server, handle non-success responses and cancellation, and log request metadata without storing secrets or unnecessary personal content. Provider-specific payloads must be checked against the selected API's current documentation.

content.task: Practice what tool calling is within function calling and tool use: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
